page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text, with the running head above it and the page number at the top right. Catchword "quod" at the lower right, gathering signature "H" at the lower left. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: ternas in aere esse sitas, non imus inficias.
Nam in quibuscunq; locis (teste Cornelio
Celso, libr. primo de Re medica) modo ca-
lor adest, modo frigus, pestilentia fit. Quod
sane septentrionales monticolæ satis experiuntur. Quæ postmodum
his subiungit Fernelius, nimirum pestilentium morborum
causam esse cœcam & occultam, & eam ta-
men esse inquinatum aerem, non recte in-
ter se cohærere videntur. Nam una & eadem
causa non potest simul esse, & euidens, &
occulta. At aër externa est causa, & propte-
rea euidens. Quod sane haud negare que-
unt Ferneliani. Nam ipsorum doctor libro
de Morborum causis, externas causas & pro-
catharticas euidentes appellat: Vbi quoq;
ex ipso euidentium genere aerem nos cir-
cumstantem esse tradit. In nos (forte) retor-
quebunt Fernelij sectatores (quos non pau-
ci, & præsertim grammaticales medicos
fore scio) non ipsum aerem nobis circum-
fusum, sed eius inquinamentum, malignā-
que qualitatem, quæ abdita est, pestis cau-
sam esse. At aeris labem esse occultam & i-
gnotam naturalis scientiæ imperitis liben-
ter concedemus, sed
hanc esse internam mor-
bi causam constanter negabimus. Id deniq;

page.notes: Page is one continuous paragraph carried over from the previous page. The running head "CAVSAS, PROGYMNASMATA." is printed in small capitals with the page number 115 at the top right. Long s has been normalised to s throughout. Line-end hyphens in "circum-fusum", "libe-nter" and "maligna-que" were joined; "morbi" is split across lines without a printed hyphen and is written whole. The text "retorquebunt" and "pauci" are read from the scan; "aër" and "aerem" are printed with the diaeresis as shown. The page ends mid-word with "deniq;" followed by the catchword "quod".
